messages.content:
A writer revised their Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China) post sentence by sentence. Compare the version before the revision with the final one, as an editor protecting what the writer meant.

Before:
<<<
大家好！我是美国人，在上海学中文已经一年了。上个周末我和朋友去杭州玩，我们在西湖旁边走路了三个小时，风景非常好看。

但是我有一个问题：我在一个饭馆点了西湖醋鱼，服务员说这个菜很有名，可是我觉得它太酸了，我不是很喜欢吃。是不是我点得不对？还有什么杭州菜你们推荐我试一试吗？谢谢！
>>>

Final:
<<<
大家好！我是美国人，在上海学中文已经一年了。上个周末我和朋友去杭州玩，在西湖边一走就是三个小时，风景美得让人舍不得停下来。

但是我有个问题想请教大家：我在一个饭馆点了西湖醋鱼，服务员说这个菜很有名，可是我觉得我吃到的这盘酸得不对劲，应该是没做好吧，我不是很喜欢吃。这道菜本来就是这个味道吗？下次再去杭州，还有哪些杭州菜值得点？你们推荐一下呗，我想试试！谢谢！
>>>

During the revision the writer confirmed what they meant at these places; changes that follow these are intended:
- 「上个周末我和朋友去杭州玩，我们在西湖旁边走路了三个小时，风景非常好看。」→ Everything this passage says now: every point, question, hedge and feeling in it stays; only how it is put changes.
- 「我有一个问题」→ Only a question about my own taste and order.
- 「但是我有个问题想请教大家：我在一个饭馆点了西湖醋鱼，服务员说这个菜很有名，可是我觉得它太酸了，我不是很喜欢吃。」→ The dish was wrong or badly cooked.
- 「是不是我点得不对？」→ Is this how the dish is supposed to taste?
- 「还有什么杭州菜你们推荐我试一试吗？」→ They want to know which Hangzhou dishes to order on their next visit to Hangzhou.

List only real problems in the final version: a point, detail, question or condition from before that is gone (lost); a claim whose meaning changed, e.g. a hedge or a hypothetical that became a flat statement (changed); text that appears twice (duplicated); a sentence that is broken where two pieces were joined (broken). Rewording, reordering and better phrasing are not problems. quote: the exact words from the final version (or, for lost, from before); note: one short English sentence to the writer, informal. [] if there is nothing.
Reply with JSON only: {"issues":[{"kind":"lost|changed|duplicated|broken","quote":"","note":""}]}
